messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH SEV - GPU hotpool (hotpath-pool-us-east1) exhausted -> >90% requests returning 429s. Auto-escalate to on-call. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/hotpool-exhaustion :rotating_light:
Alice N.: I'm oncall. seeing spikes in queue length and sustained token-bucket rejects. starting triage.
Ben C.: grabbing metrics now. QPS to hotpath up 3.6x in last 6m, avg latency for queued jobs jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s. Token bucket drop counter incrementing ~450/s.
Carla M.: any deploys or config changes in last 20m?
Dave L.: no deploys. autoscaler logs show scale-up attempts but failing due to max_replicas cap. configured max_replicas=6 for this pool. pool currently at 6.
Alice N.: ok that explains no scale. any reason cap is 6? who set it?
Ben C.: was set as a safety during last billing surge (Q4). Probably never bumped back.
OpsOncall: customer impact: internal alerting shows several enterprise customers seeing 429s on generation endpoints (~10 customers flagged). Emma S. pinged support to confirm.
Emma S.: confirmed — large finserv customer reported noticeable latency and errors for automated summaries. I'm drafting a status note.
Ben C.: digging deeper: token-bucket config for hotpath tier "strict" has refill_rate=300/s, burst=200. During surge, incoming token demand peaked ~2.5k/s. Handoff to warmpool is configured but warmpool itself saturated and warmpool scaling is constrained by same tier-policy.
Alice N.: plan: 1) temporarily increase hotpool max_replicas to 12 to relieve backlog, 2) relax tokenbucket burst and refill for hotpath tier to allow immediate smoothing, 3) enable fallback routing to cheaper model variant for non-SSO customers to reduce load. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.
Carla M.: +1 for fallback routing, but that needs careful telemetry tagging. Ben, Dave can you do 3 after we stabilize?
Ben C.: agreed. starting step 1. running admin command:
```
redwoodctl pool update --name hotpath-pool-us-east1 --max-replicas 12
```

Ben C.: API response: OK -> pool.max_replicas=12; scaling controller queued scale-up.
Alice N.: step 2 tokenbucket tweak:
```
redwoodctl tier update --name hotpath-tier --refill-rate 800 --burst 800
```

Dave L.: applied tokenbucket changes. metrics note: token_refill_rate now 800/s, burst 800.
Ben C.: scale events: new nodes coming up, 4 new GPUs provisioned in 90s; pool at 10/12 and climbing.
Alice N.: monitoring: queue length halving in last 2m, 429 rate dropping from 88% -> 18% of requests to hotpool. still a bit noisy.
Emma S.: notifying affected customers with ETA 30m for full recovery. adding note about degraded performance and automated retries.
OpsOncall: Incident timeline for customers? we need to know exact window and impacted routes.
Ben C.: logs show 429 bursts started at 1718654210 and peaked at 1718654300; spike sustained until we applied fixes at 1718654368.
Alice N.: after tokenbucket change we saw immediate drop. fallback routing not yet applied.
Carla M.: recommend follow-ups: 1) audit max_replicas settings across hot pools (several pools have conservative caps), 2) decouple tokenbucket policy between hotpath and warmpool so warmpool can scale independently, 3) add automated safety to relax tokenbucket when queue depth > threshold.
Dave L.: note: long-term, warmpool should have higher scale headroom or pre-warm policy for scheduled loads.
Ben C.: quick sanity: running smoke on affected route -> responses stable, error rate now ~1.5%.
Alice N.: ok setting incident to mitigated. Leaving thread open for postmortem items.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=mitigated, Severity=P1->P2, Mitigation=pool max_replicas increased, tokenbucket relaxed, autoscaler health recovered.
Emma S.: Customer comms: sent initial notice and will send follow-up once postmortem has RCA and ETA for config changes.
Carla M.: I'll own the postmortem and the config audit. tagging infra and runtime.
Alice N.: Action items (brief):
- Carla M.: run config audit across all hotpath pools (due EOD)
- Dave L. & Ben C.: implement decoupled tokenbucket and warmpool autoscale policy (RFC + proto by EOW)
- OpsOncall: update runbook to include "relax tokenbucket when queue > X" mitigation
- Emma S.: finalize customer follow-up and bundle metrics for impacted window

Alice N.: final note: root cause is operational config mismatch: a legacy safety cap on pool size + conservative tokenbucket tier policy blocked autoscale handoffs under sudden sustained demand. Fixes: bump headroom, decouple tiers, runbook tweak.
Ben C.: leaving monitoring hooks to catch recurrence (alert if scale blocked by cap and queue > 400).
Alice N.: thanks team. I'll hand off to next oncall in 25m.
OpsOncall: acknowledged. Handoff notes posted to /incidents/handoffs with links to metrics and the applied config diffs. :thumbsup:
Carla M.: marking follow-ups in tracker and scheduling postmortem slot.
Emma S.: will coordinate customer follow-up after postmortem.
Alice N.: handing off to OpsOncall at 1718655600 — oncall, you're up.
OpsOncall: taking over. monitoring set. closing slack incident channel thread after postmortem items are tracked. :white_check_mark:
